verdictStatement: All six findings from the v5 round are repaired, and for the first time in this lineage I could not find anything wrong with the supersession object itself. The boundedness displacement now names all three instances of the rule in both 'of' and whatIsSuperseded, the overturn clause restores all of them, the concurrence set covers every source owner including D-060 operability, and the new grant-journal lifecycle answers each of the six elements Codex's B2 enumerated. The roster holds mechanically for the second generation running: 52 changed leaf paths, zero off-roster, 132 of 132 non-roster paths byte-identical. There is no blocker. What remains is two residues of the same habit that has produced a finding in every prior round — an object gets edited and one clause inside it is left behind. In proposedSupersession, four of seven fields changed and whyNotSilent did not, so a provenance field now credits this generation with work done two generations ago and is silent on the two developments that matter most. In the new lifecycle, projectPurge is the one clause written permissively in an otherwise MUST-shaped block, which leaves the post-purge disposition of the bytes undetermined and borrows a word the artifact expressly reserves elsewhere. Neither is architectural. Both are one-line edits. But the gate is 0 and 0.

shouldFix.title: projectPurge is the one permissive clause in a MUST-shaped lifecycle, leaving the post-purge disposition undetermined, and it borrows a word the artifact expressly reserves elsewhere
shouldFix.subjectQuote: Project/operation purge does not drop grant-journal sequence. It MAY emit a terminal tombstone/archive record and then refuse further appends. Authoritative purge semantics remain DR-113.

measurement.theRetentionBoundDoesNotComposeWithIt: lifecycle.retention reads 'Sequence records are retained for the life of the project/operation identity. There is no drop bound. Archival is append-forward copy, not truncation.' If project/operation purge ends that identity, retention has expired while projectPurge forbids dropping the sequence, and nothing states what becomes of the bytes thereafter — retained indefinitely, archived, or removable. The block never says archival is required at purge; it says the writer MAY emit an archive record.
measurement.itIsTheOnlyPermissiveClause: Every other clause in the block is definite or MUST-shaped: backupRestore 'Restore MUST replay order; it MUST NOT invent or drop sequence records'; lossOrCapacity 'the writer fail-closes … MUST NOT drop or compact away order'; migration 'Historical records are not rewritten'; retention 'There is no drop bound'. projectPurge alone is optional, and it is the clause governing the one event that ends the identity the retention bound is stated against.
measurement.reservedVocabulary: The same artifact reserves the bytes 'binding retention policy and tombstones' at /bytePlacement[12], EXPRESSLY-RESERVED to DR-008 and DR-113, warranted 'File 04 GC reachability root. Evidence retention is inherit-blocked with SC-EVIDENCE.' file 04 also locates 'retention/tombstone/purge authority' in the authoritative-evidence row, not the operational-metadata row. projectPurge designs a 'terminal tombstone/archive record' without distinguishing it from the reserved object.
measurement.whatCodexAskedFor: SCC-V5-B2's repair text asked for 'project-purge inclusion/exclusion and any tombstone/archive behavior'. Inclusion is answered (purge does not drop); the tombstone/archive behavior is answered only permissively.

shouldFix.whatIsNotWrong: The lifecycle block as a whole is a real and good repair (M-8), and the reserved-bytes reading is defensible on its face: bytePlacement[12] reserves the retention-policy tombstone root, while projectPurge describes a record inside the grant journal — different bytes. I am not claiming the artifact designs reserved bytes, and 'Authoritative purge semantics remain DR-113' plus 'Mints no purge/D9 code' are correctly placed guards. The defect is that neither point is stated, so a reader must supply both distinctions themselves.
shouldFix.whyItStillMatters: The DR-124 row's acceptance cell requires 'custody, backup/purge/migration rules', and this block is labelled DESIGN-ANSWERED. A blueprint author reading it cannot decide whether purged-project journal bytes are retained forever, archived, or eventually removable, because the retention bound and the purge clause point different ways and the archival step is optional. And because the artifact reserves 'tombstones' in one field and designs a 'tombstone' in another, the same author cannot tell without inference whether that record is DR-124's to define or DR-008/DR-113's.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Make projectPurge definite: state whether a terminal tombstone/archive record MUST be emitted at purge, and state the disposition of the sequence after the project/operation identity ends — retained, archived under the append-forward rule, or removable, with the owning row named if it is not DR-124's to settle. In the same clause, distinguish this terminal journal record from the 'binding retention policy and tombstones' bytes reserved at bytePlacement[12], or rename it to avoid the collision.

coordinatorNote: This is the strongest generation of the six and the first with no blocker from me. Both of the hard things landed: the supersession now displaces the boundedness rule in all three places it lives, with overturn restoring all of them, and the grant journal has a real lifecycle whose loss and restore clauses are the right answers rather than placeholders. notFoldedThisSuccessor is accurate for the first time, which I verified against the Codex v5 bytes rather than the subject's summary. The two remaining items are the same shape as every finding I have raised since v3 — an object edited, one clause not carried along — and I would rather name that pattern once more than pretend it has gone away: whyNotSilent has now been copied forward unchanged through three generations while the object around it was rewritten twice, and projectPurge is the single permissive clause in a block that is otherwise correctly absolute. Both are one-line edits that re-decide nothing. If a v7 fixes them, I would expect to have nothing left to raise. Separately, and not as a finding: HEAD moved to D-110 mid-review, so a v7 should re-measure COORDINATOR-DECISIONS at 8daa2e6 (913eb753…) rather than carrying 72e71f2e… forward as live. I did not read the other current v6 reviewer, did not edit the subject, file 08, or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, did not apply SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL, did not mint a D-096 (A) grant, and did not commit.
